words.sense: voluntarily surrender something held or controlled
misconceptions: Giving up a role is always a formal rejection of it

words.sense: formally reject a belief, claim, or association
misconceptions: Handing over an object necessarily rejects a principle

semantic_axes.description: Giving up control of a thing or position differs from officially denying a claim, affiliation, or belief.

edges.boundary_rule: relinquish gives up something held or controlled; renounce formally rejects a belief, claim, or association.
clues_b: signs a declaration against a belief

misconceptions.M1: Any loss or handover counts as formal disavowal
misconceptions.M2: Any verbal rejection is merely a transfer of possession
misconceptions.M3: A public or difficult decision alone determines the verb

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amira’s decision about her council role?

beats.text: Amira passed the council badge and voting rights to the new leader after the election.
beats.decisive_clue: handed over an office she held
beats.reason: A transfer of responsibility is at issue.

beats.text: She was sad to leave and kept a photo of her old team.
beats.decisive_clue: gave up an office despite mixed feelings
beats.reason: Her emotions do not turn a handover into rejection of a belief.

chains.feedback_short: Key evidence: gave up an office despite mixed feelings.
chains.feedback_deep: relinquish means to let go of something one holds or controls; renounce means to formally disavow a belief, claim, or affiliation. A transfer of responsibility is at issue. Her emotions do not turn a handover into rejection of a belief.
chains.contrast_rule: relinquish gives up something held or controlled; renounce formally rejects a belief, claim, or association.

hints.attention: Notice what she actually gave up.
hints.axis: Giving up control of a thing or position differs from officially denying a claim, affiliation, or belief.
hints.contrast: relinquish gives up something held or controlled; renounce formally rejects a belief, claim, or association.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mateo’s declaration about the family house?

beats.text: Mateo signed a letter handing his sister control of the family house he had managed.
beats.decisive_clue: letter handed over authority he previously held
beats.reason: The written decision initially looks like a transfer of control.

beats.text: The same letter also formally denied that he had any rightful claim to inherit or own the house.
beats.decisive_clue: the same document formally rejected his ownership claim
beats.reason: The declaration now explicitly disavows a right, not merely control of the house.
